title: A Tale of Two Banks: When Expected Credit Loss Meets Unexpected Economic Crisis

scopes.description: Run the supplied Stata master workflow through tables 1-9 and figures 1-3. The driver includes the registered Code/ child scripts, and figure 1 creates one temporary dataset before consuming it. The run requires three distinct prepared DTA panels; none is supplied or generated by the imported source. Stata and several required commands are available, while the propensity-matching commands and regsave need setup. The blank master root also needs path configuration. No analysis-only scope is supported because the same prepared panels feed the supplied outputs.

requirements.description: Required author-prepared monthly loan-level panel loan_data_final.dta. The analyses consume the loan outcomes, bank/firm identifiers, time and treatment fields, firm covariates, loan-loss-allowance changes, risk flag and documented location indicators. The provider-to-panel producer, native date/key contract, exact allowance-change construction, and geography mapping into loan records are not supplied.

issues.description: The imported master and analysis programs consume three separate author-prepared DTA panels, none of which is in the package inventory, and no supplied program produces them. The datasheet says the authors cannot share the received raw data under their terms, while describing the underlying provincial credit-registry, Bureau of Statistics and public location-indicator sources. The data-sharing restriction does not establish that this user lacks separate provider, on-site or licensed access. The package does not provide the three panel dictionaries/producers, loan-loss-allowance calculation, area-to-loan linkage, firm-to-loan linkage, or native panel keys/periods. A selected frozen catalog search does not prove equivalent access to those prepared contracts.

The supplied master leaves global root blank and constructs do-file paths from that value. The registered child scripts are under Code/, so root must resolve to that directory (or an equivalent staged child-code directory); Stata's working directory must also resolve the bare prepared-data filenames. This is a concrete setup prerequisite, not evidence that the child scripts are absent.

evidence.description: The authors state that their data-sharing terms prohibit sharing the received raw data.
evidence.quote:
The authors will provide the editors with confidential contact information for a representative of the
   data provider who can confirm the data access arrangement, as well as copies of the relevant non-
   disclosure agreements and data sharing terms that prohibits us from sharing raw data we have
   received. Publication of aggregate summary statistics and test results is permitted. Both authors can
   vouch for the authenticity and stated sources of the raw data used in this study.

evidence.description: The datasheet says the package contains Stata programs but that the authors cannot provide code to download the proprietary raw data.
evidence.quote:
All data manipulations after obtaining the raw data were performed using computer programs. The
    replication package attached to this datasheet includes: (1) Stata code (.do files) that execute all data
    processing and statistical analyses; and (2) a Readme file that documents the execution environment,
    directory structure, package dependencies, and instructions for replication. The master.do file
    orchestrates the complete workflow from data processing through final output generation. Due to the
    proprietary nature of the raw data and the requirement to access it on-site at the data provider's offices,
    we are unable to provide code that downloads the data. The replication package documents all steps
    taken after obtaining the raw data, ensuring full transparency of our data manipulation and analysis
    procedures.

evidence.description: The datasheet names the provider and statistical office supplying the underlying loan, bank and firm source records.
evidence.quote:
We acquired loan-level and bank-level data from the Office of the China Banking and Insurance
   Regulatory Commission, which collects this information from the monthly credit registry maintained
   by all commercial banks in the province. We obtained firm-level data from the Bureau of Statistics,
   which collects financial and operational information from all registered enterprises in the province.

evidence.description: The datasheet documents the public data sources, top-five measures and date window used for its location indicators.
evidence.quote:
We constructed two location-based variables using publicly available data. The "Top 5 Infected
   Areas" indicator identifies areas among the top five in cumulative COVID-19 infection cases from
   January 1, 2020, to April 1, 2020, based on data from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and
   Prevention. The "Top 5 Restricted Areas" indicator identifies areas among the top five in lockdown
   severity from January 1, 2020, to April 1, 2020, based on population mobility data from Baidu Qianxi.
   The Baidu Qianxi platform provides real-time and historical migration patterns based on location-
   based services data, which we used to measure the reduction in traffic flow as a proxy for lockdown
   severity during the specified period. Both authors can vouch for the stated sources of the raw data.

actions.description: Establish an authorized route to the exact prepared loan panel or to its provider-approved source and producer materials.
steps: Ask for the exact prepared panel through an authorized provider or on-site route, or check whether this replication workspace holds a separate license or entitlement for the same provincial monthly credit-registry product; the authors' nonsharing term does not establish the user's access status.

For any local or licensed alternative, compare the product, record unit, required native fields, keys, periods, treatment mapping and provider terms before treating it as equivalent to loan_data_final.dta.

If only provider-approved source access is possible, request the panel dictionary, producer, joins and definitions for allowance changes, high-risk status and the area indicators. Do not infer these contracts from generic database names or reconstruct restricted credit records.
validation: After authorized acquisition, use a bounded metadata probe to check all expected native columns, file readability and reported coverage, then reconcile the exact keys, period and definitions against every consuming script before running the master driver.

actions.description: Establish authorized access to firm_data_final.dta and its provider-approved linkage/field contract.
steps: Ask for a permissioned prepared firm panel or provider-approved access to the specified provincial Bureau of Statistics records; check separately for a local license or user entitlement.

Request the native firm/time keys, variable dictionary, native date coding and coverage, treatment/exposure and risk/credit definitions, and the supported linkage to the loan panel. Do not treat a source-agency name as proof of the analysis-ready panel.
validation: After authorized acquisition, use a bounded metadata probe to verify the exact required native columns, native time keys and coverage and documented panel link before running table 1, table 9 or figure 3.

actions.description: Establish authorized access to bank_data_final.dta and its measure/key construction.
steps: Ask for the prepared bank panel or the provider-approved route to the provincial monthly credit-registry records, and check separately for a local license or user entitlement.

Request the bank identifier, observation period, treatment mapping and definitions of the size, capital, lending, interest-income and nonperforming-loan measures. Keep this requirement separate from the loan panel.
validation: After authorized acquisition, use a bounded metadata probe to check readability and required native fields, then reconcile the bank/time coverage and measure definitions before running table 1.

actions.description: If the loan panel must be rebuilt from authorized loan records, reconstruct only its public-data location indicators from the documented source families and preserve the required geographic linkage.
steps: The datasheet specifies cumulative infection cases and Baidu Qianxi migration-based lockdown severity over January 1 to April 1, 2020, with top-five area indicators. Acquire a compatible authorized public series for those exact measures and dates only if the loan panel's source mapping requires rebuilding them.
Obtain the source area identifiers and provider-approved map into the loan panel; do not use these public series as substitutes for the proprietary loan or bank observations.
validation: Verify the top-five areas, period and geographic join against the documented measure and a source-provided location crosswalk before attaching the indicators to authorized loan records.

actions.description: Configure the Stata master paths in a working copy so the registered child programs and authorized prepared data resolve without embedding a fixed author or Dropbox path.
steps: Set the master root to the directory containing the supplied table and figure do-files (the registered code folder is Code/), or stage equivalent sibling files there.

Start Stata with its working directory set to the directory containing the three authorized prepared DTA panels and desired outputs; keep this data directory distinct from the child-code root if needed.
validation: Before running any analysis, confirm by path metadata that the master include paths resolve to all twelve registered child do-files and that Stata's working directory contains each authorized input filename.

actions.description: Prepare compatible Stata commands for the propensity-score matching and diagnostic branch.
steps: Install an authorized compatible Stata package release that provides psmatch2, pstest and psgraph; retain the supplied neighbor, ties, common-support, caliper and graph options.
validation: Use bounded command metadata checks to confirm each of psmatch2, pstest and psgraph is independently discoverable in the intended Stata library; do not run the analysis source as the compatibility test.

actions.description: Prepare the Stata regsave command used by both event-study figure programs.
steps: Install an authorized compatible Stata package release that supplies regsave, preserving the supplied t-statistic, p-value and confidence-interval options.
validation: Use a bounded command metadata check to confirm regsave is independently discoverable in the intended Stata library before the user runs the figure programs.

review_notes: Static assessment only. The supplied Stata source was read through the pinned registered-source viewer; no author program or statistical model was executed.

All 17 frozen dependency checklist IDs are accounted for: D0001/D0003/D0007/D0010-D0016 map to the loan panel; D0004/D0008/D0017 to the firm panel; D0009 to the bank panel; D0002 is a generated figure1 intermediate; D0005-D0006 are master child-code calls with a concrete root setup issue.

The authors' raw-data sharing terms are recorded as their delivery restriction only. User/provider/on-site/local license access was not tested. Public infection and mobility indicators are documented as inputs to two location flags, but they are not substitutes for loan or bank observations; the exact area-to-loan mapping is not supplied.

The frozen catalog output is a selected query subset and supports candidate discovery only, not a compatible route or an exhaustive absence claim. Public repository documentation supports the reghdfe-ftools dependency; installed versions were not run against author code.

The appendix connection/configuration lines were withheld by the approved viewer; the raw Stata execution log remains opaque. Source-screen manifests and failed helper attempts remain process history and are not scientific evidence.

Datasheet title: “A Tale of Two Banks: When Credit Loss Models Meet Economic Crisis”; frozen registered title: “A Tale of Two Banks: When Expected Credit Loss Meets Unexpected Economic Crisis”. This close title variant is retained as an observation only; titles alone establish neither a separate study nor exact identity. The frozen header, DOI and provenance are unchanged.
